h1: The 7 Best Mini Chainsaws Under $100 for Pruning and Firewood, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Mini Chainsaw Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 cordless mini chainsaws under $100 compared on bar length, brushless motors, batteries and auto oilers for branch work.
summary: The SEESII 8 Inch and 6 Inch kit with two batteries and an auto oiler is the best mini chainsaw under $100 for most yards. The unbranded 1000W brushless kit is the strongest pick on motor specs, the SEESII Flagship 8-Inch is the brushless one to buy for longer cuts, and the Greenworks 24V is the safe choice if you want a known tool brand.
intro: A mini chainsaw is a pruning tool wearing a chainsaw costume, and buying it as anything bigger is the classic mistake. The bar is 6 or 8 inches, the motor is small, and the sweet spot is limbs and logs about as thick as your wrist. Ask it to fell a tree and you will burn through batteries and risk a kickback with a tool that was never designed for it.

So this ranking sorts seven under-$100 mini saws by what actually separates them in the yard: bar length, whether the motor is brushless, how many batteries come in the box, and whether the chain oils itself. We reviewed the listing titles and specs rather than inventing numbers, and where a listing says nothing about runtime or chain speed, we say so.

products.name: SEESII 8 Inch & 6 Inch Mini Chainsaw Cordless with 2 Batteries & Auto Oiler
products.verdict: Two bar sizes, two batteries and an auto oiler for under $50, which is hard to beat.
products.description:
This SEESII kit gives you both an 8 inch and a 6 inch option, two batteries and an auto oiler, and it sits in the $25 to $50 bracket. For a first mini saw that is a generous list of inclusions.

It takes the top spot because the auto oiler is the feature that keeps cheap chains alive. Mini bars run dry quickly, and a saw that feeds oil as you cut avoids the squealing, smoking, blunt-chain stage that ruins budget tools. A second battery means you can swap and carry on rather than stopping for a charge halfway through a pile of branches. It sits just above the unbranded 1000W kit because the listing is cleaner about what you get, though it does not state a motor wattage.

Buy it for general yard tidying, hedge-side limbs and small firewood. Skip it if you want a documented brushless motor for longer cuts.
products.idealFor: Homeowners trimming limbs and cutting small logs.
products.skipIf: You want a stated brushless motor.

products.name: Mini Chainsaw Cordless, 8 Inch & 6 Inch Electric Chainsaw Battery Powered, 1000W Brushless Handheld Power Chain Saw with 2 Batteries
products.verdict: A 1000W brushless motor, two bars and two batteries in one cheap kit.
products.description:
This kit lists a 1000W brushless motor, both 8 inch and 6 inch bars, and two batteries, in the $25 to $50 bracket. It is marketed for branch trimming and wood cutting.

It lands second because the brushless motor is the most important spec in this class. A brushless motor wastes less energy as heat, so a battery lasts longer and the tool bogs down less when you push into dense wood. The reason it is not first is the lack of an auto oiler in the listing, which means you will probably be oiling the chain by hand. The brand name is also less familiar, so after-sales support is harder to judge.

Pick it if you plan to cut slightly thicker branches or fill a firewood bin. Skip it if you want a tool with an established warranty or automatic oiling.
pros: Two bars cover small and mid jobs
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the strongest stated motor cheaply.
products.skipIf: You want automatic oiling and a known warranty.

products.name: SEESII Flagship 8-Inch Cordless Mini Chainsaw, Upgraded Brushless Motor
products.verdict: SEESII's upgraded brushless 8-inch saw, priced between $50 and $100.
products.description:
The Flagship is SEESII's step-up model, with an 8 inch bar and an upgraded brushless motor. Pricing runs $50 to $100, so it costs more than the kits above.

It ranks third rather than first because the listing does not state battery count or an oiler, so the extra cost does not buy extra clarity. The 8 inch bar is the real draw, since a longer bar reaches through thicker limbs in a single pass and keeps your hand further from the cut. The brushless motor should mean better efficiency than the base SEESII models.

Choose it if you want one dedicated 8 inch saw and plan on regular use. Skip it if you are happy with the cheaper dual-bar kit.
products.idealFor: Regular users who want one longer-bar saw.
products.skipIf: You want the cheapest complete kit.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 6in Mini Chainsaw, 2.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A 6 inch Greenworks saw with a 2.0 Ah battery and charger, from an established tool brand.
products.description:
The Greenworks 24V mini saw has a 6 inch bar and comes with a 2.0 Ah battery and a charger, in the $50 to $100 bracket. It runs on Greenworks' 24V battery platform, which several of the company's other tools also use.

It ranks fourth because it gives you less cutting length and a single battery against the cheaper kits. What it adds is a recognisable maker, so parts, support and a wider range of compatible batteries are easier to find. If you already own Greenworks 24V tools, an extra bare-tool battery is a quick swap.

Buy it if brand support and platform sharing matter. Skip it if you want the most bar and battery for your money.
pros: 24V battery platform shared with other tools
products.skipIf: You want two batteries and an 8 inch bar.

products.name: Cordless Mini Chainsaw Compatible with Dewalt 20V MAX Battery, 6 Inch & 8 Inch Small Electric Chainsaw Brushless, Auto Oiler
products.verdict: A brushless, auto-oiling mini saw sold as a bare tool for DeWalt 20V MAX batteries.
products.description:
This mini saw is sold as tool only, so it needs a DeWalt 20V MAX battery that you already own. It offers 6 inch and 8 inch bar options, a brushless motor and an auto oiler, and lands in the mid price tier under $100.

It ranks fifth because the price excludes a battery and charger. If you already have a DeWalt 20V MAX pack, that is a bargain, since you are paying only for a brushless, auto-oiling head. If you do not, the real cost goes well beyond the bracket shown. Compared with the Greenworks kit, it offers more bar choice and a motor type, but it is the least convenient for first-time buyers.

Ideal for anyone with spare DeWalt batteries. Skip it if you need a complete ready-to-run kit.
products.idealFor: DeWalt 20V MAX owners with spare batteries.
products.skipIf: You need a battery included in the box.

products.name: SEESII 6-Inch Mini Chainsaw Cordless with Oiler System
products.verdict: A 6 inch SEESII saw with an oiler system, in the $50 to $100 bracket.
products.description:
This model has a 6 inch bar and an oiler system. Pricing runs $50 to $100, which makes it more expensive than the dual-bar SEESII kit that includes extra batteries.

It ranks sixth because the price is high for what the listing shows. A 6 inch bar is perfectly adequate for light pruning, and the oiler helps with chain life, but the listing does not mention battery count, motor type or a second bar. The cheaper kit above gives you more in every category.

Buy it only if this exact SEESII design appeals to you. Skip it if you are comparing value, because the $25 to $50 kits cover more.
products.idealFor: Light pruners who like the SEESII layout.
products.skipIf: You want more batteries for the money.

products.name: Seesii Mini Chainsaw, 6-inch Mini Chainsaw Cordless, Handheld Electric Power Chain Saw with 2 Batteries
products.verdict: A 6 inch handheld saw with two batteries, aimed at light tree trimming and wood cutting.
products.description:
This Seesii model is a 6 inch handheld electric saw with two batteries, in the $25 to $50 bracket. The listing positions it for tree trimming, wood cutting and as a gift for a father.

It ranks last because it is the plainest kit here. There is no stated auto oiler, no brushless motor and only a 6 inch bar, so it sits below the dual-bar SEESII kit at the same price. The two batteries are the saving grace, as they give you extra working time on a small job.

Buy it as a low-risk starter saw for light branches. Skip it if you want an oiler or a stated brushless motor.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers with light trimming needs.
products.skipIf: You want an oiler or stronger motor.

whatMatters.factor: Bar length versus real cut capacity
whatMatters.detail: A 6 inch bar cuts material up to roughly 5 inches thick in practice, and an 8 inch bar stretches that a bit further. Anything bigger needs a larger saw. Check the bar size on the listing, then buy one that covers your thickest limb with a little spare.

A brushless motor controls the current electronically, which runs cooler and wastes less battery than a brushed one. That means more cuts per charge. If the listing does not say brushless, assume it is not, and expect shorter runtimes.

A chain needs oil on every cut, otherwise it overheats and dulls fast. An auto oiler feeds oil as the chain runs, so you only top up the reservoir. Without one you must stop and oil by hand, which is easy to forget.

Two batteries let you charge one while using the other. A tool-only listing like the DeWalt-compatible saw needs a battery you already own. Check what is in the box, and check the voltage matches the pack you plan to use.

Mini chainsaws kick back like larger ones, particularly when the tip hits wood. Use two hands, keep the guard in place and wear gloves and eye protection. Do not use one above shoulder height or from a ladder.

cards.text: A lightweight 6 inch or 8 inch bar, a chain oiler and a battery that lasts a few trees. Light weight matters when you reach and hold cuts at awkward angles.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: SEESII 8 Inch and 6 Inch with auto oiler suits most orchards, while the Greenworks 24V suits those who want a lighter 6 inch bar from a known brand.

cards.text: You cut every weekend or tackle limbs thicker than your wrist. The SEESII Flagship 8-Inch and its brushless motor suits that routine.

cards.text: You prune a few times a year. The SEESII 8 Inch and 6 Inch kit in the $25 to $50 bracket does the job.

faq.q: Can I use a mini chainsaw to fell a tree?
faq.a: No. These saws are for limbs, small logs and cleanup, and the bar is too short for felling. Use a full-size chainsaw or call an arborist for anything thicker than the bar length.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with mini chainsaws?
faq.a: Running the chain dry or loose. A loose chain can jump off the bar and a dry one will blunt quickly, so check tension before each session and make sure the oil tank is topped up.

faq.q: Is the Greenworks worth it over a SEESII kit?
faq.a: If you value brand support and already own Greenworks 24V tools, yes. For raw value, the SEESII kits give two batteries and an auto oiler for less, while the Greenworks has a single battery.

faq.q: Will the DeWalt-compatible saw work with any DeWalt battery?
faq.a: It is listed for DeWalt 20V MAX batteries, but it is a third-party tool, so check the adapter fit and read the seller's compatibility notes before buying. Battery and charger are not included.

faq.q: How do I look after the chain?
faq.a: Wipe off sap and sawdust after use, keep the reservoir filled with bar and chain oil, and check tension. A blunt chain should be replaced or sharpened rather than forced through the cut.
Yes. Wear cut-resistant gloves, eye protection and sturdy shoes, and keep both hands on the saw. A mini chainsaw can kick back just as a large one does.

finalTake: The SEESII 8 Inch and 6 Inch kit with two batteries and an auto oiler is the best mini chainsaw under $100 for most yards. The unbranded 1000W brushless kit wins on motor specs, the SEESII Flagship 8-Inch is the long-bar brushless pick, and the Greenworks 24V is the brand-backed option. Treat all of them as pruning tools, not felling saws, and always check for an oiler and battery count before you pay.
